title: Tailor resume to a McKinsey BA JD
persona: Yash, final-year economics, applying to consulting
scenario: You have a generic 1-page resume. The McKinsey Business Analyst JD names: structured problem-solving, leadership in college activities, comfort with quantitative analysis, and ‘entrepreneurial drive’. Your resume has a college-fest org role, a research assistant stint, a stats class project, and one freelance gig. You want a tailored version where every bullet maps to one of those 4 JD asks, but you also don't want to manufacture stories that aren't true.
badPrompt: tailor my resume for the mckinsey BA role
badOutput:
Tailored Resume:
- Led cross-functional initiatives demonstrating structured problem-solving (College Fest)
- Conducted quantitative research with statistical rigor (Research Assistant)
- Drove data-driven insights through advanced analytics (Stats project)
- Spearheaded entrepreneurial freelance ventures (Freelance gig)

hints.title: Force explicit JD mapping
hints.body: ‘Map each bullet to one of the 4 JD phrases. If a bullet doesn't map cleanly, drop it.’ Tailoring without mapping is just keyword stuffing.

hints.title: Ban manufactured drama
hints.body: ‘Don't add stories that aren't in my history. If a JD ask has no real evidence, leave it unfilled and flag it.’ Honest gaps beat fabricated bullets.

checks.tip: Force honest gap-flagging when JD ask has no evidence.
Specify a structure, bullet + JD-phrase tag + scope/metric.
Demand before/after, so you can compare what changed.

tipIfLow: JD tailoring fails when AI keyword-stuffs. The unlock is forcing explicit per-bullet JD mapping AND banning manufactured stories. If a JD ask has no real evidence, an honest gap is better than a fabricated one. McKinsey screens harder than the resume stuffer expects.
goldPrompt: Act as a resume tailor who refuses keyword stuffing. I'm Yash, final-year economics. McKinsey BA JD asks for 4 things: structured problem-solving, leadership in college activities, comfort with quantitative analysis, entrepreneurial drive. My real history: college-fest org role, research-assistant stint, stats class project, one freelance gig. Output tailored bullets where each one MAPS to one of the 4 JD phrases — tag the mapping at the end like [→ structured problem-solving]. If a JD ask has no real evidence, leave the slot UNFILLED and flag it [GAP — discuss in interview]. Refuse to manufacture stories.
